caveats: ||h|| here is the norm of the POSITION-MEAN hidden state, not the mean of per-position norms — that is what is banked. Averaging over positions cancels position-varying components, so these are LOWER than a per-position ||h||. Both arms are reduced identically, so the ratio (the load-bearing quantity) is fair, but the absolute fractions should not be quoted as 'the injection displaces X% of the residual stream'.

The two models' sites are at matched RELATIVE depth (8/28, 15/28, 19/28, 22/28 vs 9/32, 17/32, 21/32, 25/32), not matched absolute layer index. That is deliberate and is how both maps were built; it is also why a site-for-site ratio is the right comparison.

The corpora differ (w6 wide vs corpus_8b), so this ratio mixes model scale with corpus composition. It is an upper bound on the purely-model part, which is the conservative direction for an error bar.

The reference BAND this is used with (w5_r32_measured.json) was measured on a different 3B map than the corpus these 3B ||h|| come from (w6 wide). That is fine for the denominator: ||h|| is a property of the MODEL at a site, not of the map, and [8, 15, 19, 22] is the project-wide 3B site set that every 3B map including w5 uses (inherited from B1 -- LEDGER-ideas-and-outcomes.md). loom_map_w5_r32.npz is no longer on disk anywhere reachable, so its own corpus's ||h|| cannot be measured; if it reappears, re-measure and check this ratio.
